This test is defined on `ReceiptTests`, whose `setUp` patches `receipt.validate_append` with a no-op mock (lines 16-20). Therefore the base test run never raises `AdmissionError` and fails unconditionally; the real validator is only restored by the `PublisherAdmissionTests` subclass. Move this control to the real-engine integration class (or provide a deterministic validation stub that raises for MD012) so the ordinary suite does not assert an exception that its fixture disables.

Disproved against exact head `fead02555f0b8f6fb70b3c351a7f34ef1bb29c08`. Both new methods belong to `PublisherAdmissionTests`, not `ReceiptTests`. Its `setUp` calls the shared fixture and then explicitly calls `self.admission.stop()`, restoring the real `validate_append`. The exact published negative method passes with the adopted engine and zero skips; all31 publisher controls pass, including16 real-engine integrations. Against the unchanged adopted source, the positive leading-blank control fails with actual `AdmissionError: markdown_new_findings MD012:5`, while the excessive-blank negative control passes. That sensitivity result depends on active validation, not a no-op mock. Evidence is retained in `leading-red.log` and `publisher-green.log` under the owned Mini qualification root. Current-head SFL Round1 PASS and canonical unit/Markdown checks are also complete. No test or production edit was made in response to this incorrect class attribution.
